# Why can't we simply splash naked foreign DNA onto plant cells to change their traits?

Suppose we extract a useful gene—such as drought resistance—and bathe intact plant cells in a solution containing naked DNA strands.

We might assume cells absorb the DNA like a sponge.

Instead, the rigid outer plant cell wall acts as an impenetrable physical barrier. Naked DNA floating outside is also degraded by cellular enzymes before reaching the interior.
